dct_description_sm: The overarching objective of this project was to quantify the contribution of snowmelt runoff to the metal mass balance of Arctic tundra lakes.  This work contributes new knowledge and research on pathways and processes of metals in Arctic tundra landscapes.  Specifically, the  study provides important insight into the role of snow hydrology in coupling atmospheric sources of trace metals, including inorganic and methyl-mercury, to Arctic freshwaters.  Snow hydrology is potentially a key component of current ecosystem changes in the Arctic that may influence metal levels and trends in monitored species.  Two spring field measurement campaigns were undertaken over the spring melt periods of 2014 and 2015 to quantify the trace metal mass balance for a small lake near the community of Iqaluit. The information collected is contributing to the important, long-term objective of understanding and predicting how climate and ecosystem changes will affect trace metal fate, transport and food web bioaccumulation in Arctic freshwaters.  The specific scientific questions of this research were as follows:  1) What are trace metal loads in snowpack just prior to spring snowmelt in Arctic tundra watersheds on Southern Baffin Island? 2) What is the fate of trace metal loads from snowmelt runoff? Do metal inputs mix in the water column, deposit to lake-bottom sediments, or exit the lake via the outflow?  3) How much do snowmelt loads contribute to total metal loads in Arctic tundra lakes?  Landscape snow water equivalent and metal concentrations, including total mercury, methyl-mercury, lead and cadmium in snowpack and snowmelt runoff were quantified over two spring snowmelt periods (2014 and 2015) and the corresponding contributions to 6 lakes in the vicinity of the community of Iqaluit, NU.  A nearby lake was  monitored and sampled continuously until late October for a comprehensive water and metal mass balance, to understand controls of lake hydrology and mixing on metal dynamics in the water column throughout spring snowmelt periods.
dct_title_s: General chemistry, trace metal concentrations and isotopic composition of snow and surface waters during the spring snowmelt period, Iqaluit, Nunavut, 2014-2015
